title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class mixed add/square rho on GT (revision v5)

claims.statement: For uniform z in GT and uniform nonidentity input (the challenge of rules.md), the algorithm in proof.md returns P with e(P, Q) = z with probability at least 0.41, using at most 2^125.789684 target-group-operation equivalents (score 31447421/250000) counting every operation of the procedure (a hard work cutoff), with preprocessing 2^76.418283. Peak memory is at most 2^73.166564 bytes (a distinguished-point table with an overflow stop). Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. An adder step is charged 1 (the reference operation) plus the other instructions divided by C; a square step is charged the cyclotomic square (kappa = 0.4902) plus the other instructions divided by C, with the instruction counts measured by Callgrind on the organizer's blst build. The bound rests on the stated heuristics H1, H5 and H7 and on the derived bounds in proof.md. This is a classical generic attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the Frobenius-class mixed walk (cscore.gt) on toy order-ell subgroups of F_{q^12}^* with ell dividing q^4 - q^2 + 1, solve each instance end to end and verify g^y = z, and compare the success curve of tau = T^2 V / (2N) with 1 - exp(-tau), reporting cycle rates. Toy scale only: it tests H1 and the solver, not production cost.

Recompute the claimed time_log2 (hard work cutoff with its charge bounds), the failure terms, the success bound, preprocessing, and memory, from the stated parameters, the measured c2 and kappa, and cscore.exact.
